description: Fix one() and only() discarding custom exceptions whose instances are falsy. A supplied exception must be raised by identity; formatting a default message must not evaluate item repr when a custom exception was supplied. Add regression tests.
acceptance: Exercise too_short and too_long with falsy exception instances, items with failing repr, and default errors. Preserve existing iterator consumption behavior.

description: Add public random_ordered_range(*args), yielding every value of range(*args) once in shuffled order. Support the standard range forms and invalid arguments. Keep auxiliary storage bounded for huge ranges; this is a practical randomized traversal, not a cryptographic or uniform-over-all-permutations promise. Integrate exports, type stub, README, API documentation and tests.
acceptance: Match range values for positive, negative, empty and stepped inputs; iterator API; invalid step rejected; sampling the beginning of a billion-item range must not allocate the whole range. Small inputs must have varied orders. Existing tests pass.

description: Investigate why reversed(numeric_range(...)) can disagree with reversing its forward values for fractional steps and can overflow near datetime boundaries. Diagnose the root cause in a short docs/evaluation-debug.md, fix it and add regressions without materializing the range.
acceptance: list(reversed(r)) equals list(r)[::-1] for float positive/negative steps, Decimal, Fraction and datetime near min/max. Reversal remains lazy and compatible with existing tests.

description: Simplify nth_permutation for partial permutations. It currently computes a factorial-based full-permutation rank then discards work; eliminate those unnecessary computations while preserving public behavior. Add exhaustive small-input equivalence tests against itertools.permutations and a large-n/small-r regression.
acceptance: Preserve lexicographic ordering, negative indices, empty r and errors for invalid r/index. Avoid computing factorial(n) for partial permutations. Existing tests pass; demonstrate the simplification in code and regression tests.

description: Repair seekable's zero-cache mode (maxlen=0) comprehensively. peek and bool must not drop elements, repeatable lookahead must preserve next/list behavior, and the lookahead mechanism must use bounded memory across long streams. Check seek/relative_seek interactions and preserve ordinary bounded/unbounded replay semantics. Add behavior and memory regressions and docs/evaluation-seekable.md explaining invariants and tradeoffs.
acceptance: Repeated peek/bool do not consume values, next yields the peeked object, exhaustion/default semantics work, elements() stays empty with maxlen=0, long non-cached streams do not accumulate storage. Existing seekable and full-suite tests pass. Tests cover normal maxlen None/1/3 replay and forward/relative seeks. Durable explanation and tests must remain sufficient to continue after interruption.
